title: The Roman Empire: Government and Administration
text: The Roman Empire was governed by an emperor who held absolute power, supported by a Senate that served an advisory role. The empire was divided into provinces, each governed by a governor (proconsul or legate) appointed by the emperor or Senate. Roman law was highly developed and codified, with the Corpus Juris Civilis under Emperor Justinian in the 6th century CE representing a major compilation. Roman citizenship was gradually extended to provincials, culminating in the Edict of Caracalla (212 CE), which granted citizenship to all free men in the empire. The Roman army, the legions, was the backbone of Roman power and control.
